notes:
Government: City of Charlottesville, Virginia (independent city; not part of Albemarle County). Official site: https://www.charlottesville.gov. Researched 2026-10-10 by Claude (claude-opus-5-5), discovery pass: read-only fetches of official pages; each process carries one verbatim quote checked by script against the fetched page text. Status: discovery (not yet a researched answer); details per process still need a full research pass before publishing.

Method: the site sitemap (https://www.charlottesville.gov/sitemap.xml, 1,151 URLs) plus the How Do I, Get, Pay, Report, Request and Submit pages, the Departments A-H and L-V lists, every department landing page in the Departments lists, the Commissioner of the Revenue Forms Index, the FormCenter index, Utility Billing forms, the utility fee schedule, the building permit fee pages, the Development Requirements page, and selected FAQ pages. About 401 pages and one PDF (New Business License Checklist) were fetched with User-Agent 'lexflow-research/0.1 (https://github.com/alibama/lexflow)' at no more than one request per 1.25 seconds per host. Nothing was submitted, no account was created, and no one was contacted.

Quotes: each process has exactly one evidence quote, copied from the cited page's fetched text and checked by script (whitespace-normalised substring match). Some quotes are a form or link title when the page had no fuller sentence. State law appears only as citation hints (citation, title and URL from the lexflow 'va' index); none is quoted, and no hint has been checked against the process in detail. Local code sections are listed only where an official city page names them.

Frequency levels (very_common, common, occasional, rare) and their text are estimates from city size (about 46,000 residents, large university population) and the scale shown on pages. They are not city statistics.

Privacy: no staff names, named officials' direct lines or personal-looking mailboxes are recorded. Several city pages name individual staff and give personal mailboxes (for example the Assessor appeal and income-expense pages, the Downtown Mall page, Traffic Engineering, and many FormCenter 'Email Contact Form for <name>' forms); those were left out and only office titles kept. The Police home page shows missing-person and arrest notices; none of that was recorded.

robots.txt: boards.charlottesville.gov (Boards and Commissions, BZA, BAR and Planning Commission pages) disallows all crawling. Three board pages were refused by the fetcher. One page on that host was fetched by mistake when a www.charlottesville.gov link (/235) redirected there; its content was not used. Board URLs appear here only as links shown on city pages.

Out of scope or separate bodies (not city processes, so not listed): Charlottesville City Schools enrollment, Jefferson-Madison Regional Library, University of Virginia (own parking, police and FOIA), Albemarle County. Regional bodies that serve city residents appear where city pages send residents to them: Rivanna Solid Waste Authority, JAUNT, the Emergency Communications Center, the Blue Ridge Cigarette Tax Board (TJPDC), the Thomas Jefferson Soil and Water Conservation District and the Virginia Department of Taxation.

Courts: the Circuit, General District and Juvenile and Domestic Relations courts are state courts that sit in the city. Their clerks' processes listed here come from the city's court pages and the vacourts.gov court pages. No city or court page described probate, name changes, concealed handgun permits, notary commissions or assumed-name certificates at the Circuit Court Clerk; these Clerk services exist under state law but were not added as processes without an official page to cite.

Searched for but not found on the site: an alarm ordinance or false-alarm fee, fire code operational permits, open-burning permits, a rental inspection program, noise or amplified-sound permits, block-party permits, buying a cemetery plot, and local candidate filing deadlines. Fingerprinting is currently suspended by the Police Department. Rent relief, real estate tax relief and CHAP applications are closed for the current cycle, according to their pages.

Data quirks to check in the research pass: the Dog Tags page cites 'City of Charlottesville Code Section 3.2-65', which matches Virginia Code Title 3.2, Chapter 65 rather than a city section. The Income and Expense page still shows a 2023 deadline. The floodplain page links 'City Code Section 34-256' and 'City Ordinance 34-240', which may be pre-2024 zoning numbers. The Personal Property FAQ gives the real estate rate (applied to mobile homes) as $0.98, while the Treasurer's Real Estate Taxes page says $0.99.
